correctness.rationale: Eliminating juveniles yields the stated constant-coefficient equation and initial derivative −α. The positive decay roots r<s satisfy (α−r)(α−s)=−βκ<0, so the adult trajectory is a strictly decreasing convex combination of the two decays. For the difference, combine repeated exponents first. On any finite interval a nonzero sum of m distinct real exponentials has at most m−1 zeros with multiplicities, by factoring out one exponential and applying Rolle to the derivative, which has one fewer term. With at most four terms the common zero at t=0 leaves at most two positive zeros; if α is equal the initial zero is at least double, leaving at most one. For the canonical family direct trace/determinant evaluation gives decay pairs {1,3} and {2,4}; the spectral weights are p and q and both juvenile nonmaturation losses are strictly positive. For x=e^(−t), the residual factor in x(1−x)[p+(p−q)x+(1−q)x²] equals x(1+x)(g_p(x)−q), with g_p(x)=p/x+x/(1+x). On (0,1), g_p either strictly decreases (p≥1/4) or decreases to one interior minimum 2√p−p and increases to p+1/2 at the right endpoint. This gives exactly the claimed strict window and the two boundary degeneracies; the coincident endpoint p=1/4 is not in the open window. At p=1/10, q=11/20 the residual quadratic is (3x−1)(3x−2)/20, giving exactly the stated ordered times and signs. All claims are for expected adult trajectories with common adult-only initialization, not for total populations or sample paths.
residual_risks: The numerical script was inspected, not executed; the analytical proof does not require sampling. No empirical model fit or wider ranking result is established.

value.rationale: Even monotone decline and a common adult-only baseline do not preserve census rankings. A sharp, biologically feasible witness and all phase boundaries for the simple equally spaced four-mode comparison supply a reproducible benchmark for when snapshot rankings can mislead. This is distinct from restating the classical exponential zero bound.
residual_risks: Idealized linear expectation benchmark, not empirical relevance or prediction for stochastic sample paths.
